en: The Scripture of the One-Syllable Extraordinary Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa,
Volume One. By the Duke of Sui, who held the rank of Kaifu Yitongsigong, the Special Advancement (Teci), the Acting Minister of State Ceremonial (Shi Hongluqing),
with an appanage of three thousand households, invested in purple robes, and posthumously honored as Minister of Justice (Sisi).

Translated by the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, Tripitaka Master of the Great Xingshan Monastery, who was posthumously honored with the title "Great Rectifier of the Canon" and "Great One of Vast Wisdom," by Imperial Decree. Chapter One: Manifesting Majestic Power and Virtue. Thus have I heard.

At one time, the Bhagavān was dwelling in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven in the Universal Radiance Pavilion, which was produced by the immeasurable merit empowered by the Tathāgata and adorned with millions of great blessings.
The great merit of the Buddha’s accumulations is universally praised as immeasurable;
it is a multitude of countless virtues.
Immeasurable Vajra,
the firm and indestructible place,
the adornment of the pure Buddha-world.
All the kingly mani jewels are adorned with blossoming ornaments, perfectly pure and radiant,
and take delight in wisdom.
Stainless, radiant, and blazing maṇi jewels,
beautifully adorned,
extending throughout the world-systems.
The samādhi is perfectly pure;
the exposition of the principles of all phenomena is pure;
and it is interspersed with vast oceans of mani-jewels of immeasurable colors.
He manifested the inexhaustible samādhi of the Tathāgatas,
with pure, inexhaustible kingly maṇi jewels interspersed with transformed flowers.
Adorned with swirling currents of mani-jewel tree branches,
they skillfully manifest the wisdom of the Buddha through expedient means.
It was interlaced with the radiance of all kinds of flower fragrances and mani-jewels,
blazing everywhere;
it was the universal light manifested through the playful supernatural powers (ṛddhi-vikrīḍita) sustained by the Buddha’s empowerment.
Within this great celestial palace, all mani-jewels turn extensively and universally;
it is observed from the ten directions and adorned with various treasures such as vaidūrya.
It was surrounded by stairways and pathways of immeasurable jewel-kings interlaced together,
with various mani-jewels and pearls hanging down as pendants;
it was adorned with upright canopies, banners, and streamers of exquisite beauty.
It was covered with nets of pearls and jewel-nets spread over precious canopies;
it was adorned with the application of dragon-firm sandalwood and inlaid with sovereign-kings jewels.
A net of maṇi jewels completely covers it;
the ground is established by the Victorious Dragon,
adorned through and through with the universal radiance of wisdom.
It was draped with nets of mani-jewel pillars interlaced together;
it was covered by śāla trees made of the lion-essence mani-jewel king;
and it had gates of the supreme lion-banner mani-jewels.
The windows of the lands are wonderfully adorned,
reflecting one another without obstruction;
there are *māndārava* flowers and *mahāmāndārava* flowers.
Mañjūṣaka flowers and great mañjūṣaka flowers;
roca flowers and great roca flowers;
cakra flowers and great cakra flowers.
Sumanā flowers, mañjūṣaka flowers,
tālīsa flowers, mallikā flowers,
kunda flowers, and saptaparṇa flowers.
He scattered *dhanuṣkāri* flowers, celestial *sumana* flowers, *utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*,
and white lotus flowers of great size.
Seated upon the lion throne of the treasury adorned with undefiled wisdom,
his sublime and pure intelligence manifests non-duality;
he proclaims the dharma of signlessness and abides in the dwelling of the Buddhas.
They attain equality with all Buddhas,
unimpeded penetration of the non-retrogressive Dharma,
and inconceivable purity of an unsurpassable realm.
He has attained a body that is equal throughout the three periods of time and pervades all worlds;
his cranial protuberance (uṣṇīṣa) cannot be seen by anyone;
and he possesses the wisdom that is free from doubt regarding all phenomena.
He has accomplished the wisdom of all practices;
he possesses unerring awakened knowledge and a non-conceptual body.
Abiding in non-dual wisdom, he dwells in the most supreme perfection.
The Tathāgata possesses indestructible wisdom and the wisdom of liberation;
having ultimately realized equality that is without center or periphery,
he possesses effortless wisdom that exhausts the entirety of space and pervades the whole Dharma-realm.
He attained all Buddha-activities throughout all future eons, infinite and countless,
through the empowerment of turning the non-retrogressive wheel and proceeding to the site of enlightenment to subdue Māra.
Having realized perfect enlightenment, he turns the wheel of Dharma;
he manifests the treasury of unattached wisdom,
perfected in all aspects, invulnerable to any influence, and free from dependence.
He is skillfully able to manifest instantaneously throughout all worlds in the ten directions,
dwelling in the Tuṣita heaven palace,
and manifesting his passing away, birth, renunciation, ascetic practices, and preparatory applications.
Proceeding to the site of enlightenment to subdue Māra;
manifesting the realization of enlightenment and turning the wheel of Dharma;
entering parinirvāṇa and abiding in the concealment of the Dharma.
Together with forty thousand bhikṣus and eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas,
all of whom had come from the worlds of the ten directions,
they had all reached the stage of being destined for one more birth (ekajātipratibaddha) and attained the position of consecration (abhiṣeka).
He gives birth to immeasurable samādhis and liberations.
He abides in the supreme vajra samādhi and attains the supreme lotus samādhi.
Upon attaining the vajra-like samādhi,
one sports with the supreme ornaments of the victory banner,
and all Buddha-dharmas manifest before one.
He dwells in the samādhi of the Adornment of the Treasury of Merits;
he abides securely in the site of enlightenment in the happy realms and enters the sphere of the Buddhas.
He has attained the adornment of all demonic spheres through the most supreme physical marks by means of the dhāraṇī of inexhaustible speech.
Having attained the inexhaustible phrases, they proclaim the prediction of enlightenment during the non-empty eon;
they are able to crush the evil multitudes of other teachings,
establishing a reputation praised throughout the ten directions.
He gave birth to immeasurable generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, and skillful means,
which were praised and extolled by all Buddhas for incalculable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas.
Having perfected their activities, they distance themselves from the profound and unfathomable law of dependent origination;
entering into the extreme views of eternalism and nihilism,
they are able to inflict the diseases of affliction upon all sentient beings.
Possessing a thoroughly purified, pristine, upright, and stainless intention that knows the medicinal remedies for phenomena as they correspond to each case,
and endowed with courageous, firm, adamantine, and indestructible benevolence.
He is able to gather and instruct all sentient beings with impartial wisdom;
his immeasurable merit and knowledge pervade the limits of space.
Abiding in the principle of the eloquence of the *daśabala-dhāraṇī*,
namely the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
the Constantly Contemplating Avalokiteśvara.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta,
the Bodhisattva Vijñānagati,
and the Bodhisattva Vajramati.
The Bodhisattva Siṃhamati,
the Bodhisattva Siṃhavikrāntagāmin,
and the Bodhisattva Vajravikrāntagāmin.
The Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
the Bodhisattva Vajraketu,
and the Bodhisattva Akṣobhyavikramaparākrama.
The Bodhisattva Pure Eye;
the Bodhisattva Courageous Steadfastness in the Steps of the Three Times;
and the Bodhisattva Lotus Ornament.
The Bodhisattva Padmanetra,
the Bodhisattva Ratnavyūha,
and the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
The Bodhisattva Stainless Space,
the Bodhisattva Wondrous Arm,
and the Bodhisattva Wondrous Wisdom.
The Bodhisattva Mahāmati,
the Bodhisattva Ratnagarbha,
and the Bodhisattva Ratnadhvaja.
The Bodhisattva Ratnamudrāhasta,
the Bodhisattva Śrīrājapratibhāsa,
and the Bodhisattva Guṇarājapratibhāsa.
The Bodhisattva King of Adornment,
the Bodhisattva Adorned with Lightning Radiance,
and the Bodhisattva Treasury of Space.
The Bodhisattva Destroyer of Doubt,
the Bodhisattva Cloud Sound,
and the Bodhisattva Pure Wisdom.
With Bodhisattva Thunderous Sound,
the youthful Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī,
and Bodhisattva Maitreya as their leaders.
Together with all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the Bhadrakalpa,
there were also the devaputra Subhaviṣaya and the devaputra Jayamāra.
The devaputra Guṇavyūha,
the devaputra Jaya,
and the devaputra Śāntavinīteśvara.
The Devaputra Jñānavijaya,
the Devaputra Sucintita,
and other such devaputras of great majestic power, together with twenty thousand devaputras.
They all gave rise to the bodhicitta and planted roots of goodness.
Furthermore, there were the gods of the Four Heavenly Kings and the various classes of devas.
Śakra, Lord of Devas; the Deva Sārthavāha;
and Maheśvara, the Deva.
Brahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World;
Māra, the Son of Heaven;
and furthermore, a great assembly of śrāvakas.
Namely, Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana,
and Kātyāyanīputra.
Pūrṇa, Piṇḍola, and Gavāmpati.
The stupas of the venerable elders:
Kāśyapa and Mahākāśyapa.
Gaya-Kāśyapa, Rāhula, and others such as these were their leaders.
Furthermore, there were five thousand great yakṣa generals,
namely the yakṣa general Pūrṇabhadra and the yakṣa general Maṇibhadra.
The yakṣa general Śarabha, the yakṣa general Nāhala,
and the yakṣa general Pañcika.
Together with the Mother Hariti and her five hundred sons as her retinue,
all the kings of mountains and great rivers,
and the Garuda as their leader.
There were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of garuḍa kings,
as well as tree kinnara kings with immeasurable kinnaras as their retinues,
and Nārāyaṇa, the lord of all living beings.
The lord of spirits, Īśāna,
with his immeasurable hundreds of thousands of retinues,
together with the Naga King Vasuki.
The Naga King Padma,
the Great Naga King Mahāpadma,
and the Naga King Sāgara were their leaders.
He was accompanied by a retinue of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of nāga kings,
as well as other devas, nāgas, yakṣas, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans.
At that time, the World-Honored One, surrounded before and behind by an assembly of immeasurable hundreds of thousands,
sat upon the Greatly Adorned Lion Throne and initiated the recitation of the mantra of the Tathāgata’s Crown.
His roar was like that of a lion;
his radiance was like the sun; his brilliance was like the moon;
his pervasive illumination was like Śakra; and his intensity was like a blazing torch.
Its light is like that of Brahmā, and its loftiness is like Mount Sumeru;
it is greater than the ocean. Thus the sequence of the mantra practice for the Buddha’s Uṣṇīṣa is taught.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bodhisattvas and others, saying:
Noble son, there is a supreme king of all samādhis of all Tathāgatas.
By abiding in this samādhi,
one becomes the One-Syllable Wheel King Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa.
You should listen attentively, listen well, and listen most excellently; apply your minds with earnestness and uphold this.
By upholding it, a bodhisattva shall not regress from unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Then all the great bodhisattvas joined their palms and addressed the Buddha, saying,
"We pray only that the World-Honored One will expound the single syllable of the Great Vidyārāja.
At that time, the World-Honored One entered the King of Samādhis of All Supreme Victors.
He spoke this vidyārāja:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ* *phurūṃ hūṃ*. As soon as he had spoken this vidyārāja, throughout the trichiliocosm...
It becomes a net of light,
universally illuminating worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River,
shining upon all those worlds.
It causes all those worlds to tremble.
All Tathāgatas enter into all samādhis, the sovereign king of samādhis,
and they also proclaim this Great Vidyārājñī.
When it was spoken, it was heard everywhere.
This trichiliocosm shook in six ways:
the east rose and the west sank; the south rose and the north sank.
It surged upward and plunged downward, shaking and trembling violently.
All the devas rose from their seats and approached the presence of the Tathāgata,
continuing thus up to the assembly of the Akaniṣṭha heaven.
They all directed their thoughts toward the Tathāgata,
as did all sentient beings within the trichiliocosm, including those in the hells,
the animal realm, and the realm of Yama.
By virtue of being touched by the light of the King of Pinnacle Radiance,
all painful sensations were eliminated;
at that time, sentient beings were free from malice and regarded one another as they would their own parents.
All those sentient beings born therein perceive one another in this way:
within the trichiliocosm, they see the Cakravāḍa Mountains,
the Mahācakravāḍa Mountains, and other Black Mountains.
Because this vidyārāja’s uṣṇīṣa radiates brilliant light,
it extends downward as far as the Great Avīci Hell and upward as far as the Akaniṣṭha Heaven.
All the great supernormal powers, great majesty, and great sovereignty of the sun and moon were eclipsed and could not shine;
there was not a single place that was not pervaded by their radiant light.
Thus, by means of the supernormal power of the Blessed One’s divine conduct,
those who were insane regained their mindfulness, the blind regained their sight,
the mute regained the ability to speak, and the lame became able to walk.
The deaf shall hear; the naked shall obtain clothing.
Whatever they seek—food, drink, and all necessary provisions—they shall obtain.
Those who suffer shall find peace and security.
Even those who were pregnant attained safety at the time of delivery.
Then, those bodhisattvas approached the World-Honored One;
filled with wonder, they spoke these words:
“World-Honored One, this Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa-Rāja is inconceivable, marvelous, extraordinary,
and most wondrous. World-Honored One, you have acted thus,
beholding this trichiliocosm.”
A net of jewels covered everything above.

From the sky there rained down exquisite celestial flowers, clouds of celestial flowers, clouds of powdered incense, clouds of sandalwood, clouds of garments and ointments, clouds of flower garlands, and clouds of exquisite celestial flower garlands.
All the bodhisattvas, as well as all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others,
scattered exquisite celestial flowers over the Buddha.
Furthermore, silken garments, precious parasols, banners, and streamers rained down,
while celestial music played in the sky;
from that music issued forth such sounds as these:
How marvelous is the Buddha’s Uṣṇīṣa, O World-Honored One!
Even Bodhisattvas dwelling on the ten stages cannot behold it;
yet all sentient beings mutually obtain peace and happiness through it.
They attained the samādhi of mindfulness of the Buddha.
At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra and all the sons of the gods of the entire desire realm went together to the World-Honored One and addressed the Buddha, saying:
Blessed One, if there be anyone who upholds this Great Vidyārājñī,
all of us gods, upon seeing them,
shall rise and offer them half of our own seats to sit upon.
Then the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
"Lord of the Devas, it is the natural law that one who has accomplished the Uṣṇīṣacakravartin..."
When Śakra, Lord of Devas, and the other gods see [this practitioner], they will certainly share their seats with him.
Since Śakra, Lord of Devas, is not included within the realm of sentient beings,
he would not grant even half a seat to one who has not achieved the Uṣṇīṣacakravartin.
Except for Bodhisattvas who have attained the stages,
those who dwell in the inconceivable liberation and have attained samādhi,
as well as Pratyekabuddhas and Śrāvakas who are free from desire.
It is the natural law of the Lord of Devas that if anyone else, having accomplished the Cakravartin, does not rise from their seat,
their head shall split into a hundred pieces.
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, spoke these words:
"World-Honored One, I shall provide protection for the upholder of the vidyā who practices,
recites, or makes offerings to this Vidyārāja."
If one copies the sūtra scrolls or even upholds them,
they shall not fall into the evil realms,
and it will cause them to attain right mindfulness.
The World-Honored One praised Śakra, Lord of the Devas:
"So it is, so it is, Śakra! If there should be one who accomplishes this vidyārāja, or one who recites it..."
They will certainly not fall into the evil realms;
they will attain the knowledge of past lives, be free from flattery and crookedness, and refrain from divisive speech.
They will not be hypocritical, will possess no double-mindedness, and will be endowed with skillful means.
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, who holds the Uṣṇīṣa-cakra,
will never fall into the evil destinies;
he shall always be born into the clans of Brahmins or Kṣatriya great kings.
He was handsome, endowed with excellent physical marks and signs;
he achieved mastery in literature, rhetoric, and the arts;
and he was free from stinginess.
One attains the power of hearing and retaining [the teachings] without forgetting;
it is the natural law that one is never separated from one's parents.
The majestic power of the Buddha’s Uṣṇīṣa is inconceivable, peerless, and immeasurable.
The Buddha-Usnīṣa family is inconceivable.
At that time, all those hosts of devas and bodhisattvas were struck with wonder,
for they had made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas.
It shall come into the hands of that person, being embraced by all the celestial worlds;
once it has reached that person's hands, it shall not be destroyed.
Whoever obtains this shall accomplish inconceivable merit.
Chapter Two: The Chapter on Mudrās. From the *Ekākṣara-uṣṇīṣa-citrasūtra*, Chapter Two, the Chapter on Mudrās.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi was surrounded by an immeasurable koṭi of vidyādharas.
He went to the World-Honored One, prostrated with his head at the Buddha's feet,
and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, there is a great upholder of vidyā-mantras."
Regarding those who practice the mantra path of the Buddha's teachings but lack skillful means and do not understand the ritual protocols,
for the benefit of such sentient beings, they shall swiftly attain accomplishment through these skillful means.
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will expound the teachings of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mantra.
The Buddha told Vajrapāṇi:
"The vidyādhara should first receive the three refuges and generate the bodhicitta."
Having purified oneself through ritual bathing and with great compassion for all sentient beings,
one should form the mudrās in a secluded place,
receiving them by personally hearing the instructions from the master.
If one forms a bond other than this,
various malevolent spirits and vināyakas will create obstacles and difficulties, leading to death and a fall into hell;
this applies to those who have not received empowerment and those who have not generated the bodhicitta.
That person should not first bind these mudrās; rather,
they should first bind the heart-mudrās of the three families,
joining the four tips with one another.
With both wheels held upright and the front fingers joined together,
this is called the Heart Seal of all Tathāgatas.
Then, with the previous mudrā, bend the left wheel into the palm;
keep the right wheel upright as before.
This is called the Heart-mantra of the Lotus Family.
This is the same heart-seal of the Padmakula as before; however,
the right wheel is bent and inserted into the palm,
while the left wheel remains upright as previously described.
This is called the Heart Seal of the Vajra Family.
With both hands held upright and crossed at the tops,
join the palms with hollowed fingers like a flower held within the palms.
This is the universal seal of all Buddha-uṣṇīṣas.
Vajragarbha, you should first form the seal of the Universal Monarch (Cakravartin), the sovereign of all Buddha-uṣṇīṣas, which is the supreme among all mundane and supramundane mantras.
Interlace the two hands within to form fists;
extend the two *raśmis* (index fingers) with their upper joints bent,
and hold the two wheels (*cakras*) side by side and upright.
Bend the two joints of both hands and rest them against the two wheels;
this is the fundamental mudrā of the Wheel-Turning King (Cakravartin).
The most excellent among all mudrās is the aforementioned root mudrā;
place the right hand behind the right light.
Holding it perfectly upright so that it does not touch [the ground],
this is called the *mūrdha-mudrā* (Crown Seal);
it is identical to the previously mentioned root seal (*mūla-mudrā*).
The two *kaṣāyas* (robes) are each placed upright behind the light so that they do not touch one another;
this is called the head seal (*mūdrā*).
This is the same as the previous root mudrā;
however, with both hands inverted, bend the two thumbs back against the two index fingers.
This is the armor mudrā (*kavaca-mudrā*).
This is the same as the previous root mudrā;
bend the second joints of the two thumbs so that their backs press against each other.
With both hands held level and upright, attach two seals [to the thumbs].
This is the mudrā of the wall.
By forming this mudrā, the vidyādhara [achieves his purpose].
If even those who practice at the crown of the head and so forth cannot approach,
how much less can other obstructing vināyakas do so?
This refers to the aforementioned root mudrā.
Bending the two thumbs to support the two index fingers at the third joint—
this is called the Wheel-Turning King’s Heart-Seal (*cittamudrā*).
When conjoined with the mantra, it is capable of accomplishing all ritual activities.
This is the same as the previous root mudrā;
however, bend the two thumbs and attach them to the third joints of the two index fingers.
This is called the Cakravartin Heart-to-Heart Mudrā.
Then, using the same fundamental mudrā as before,
bend the right hand and place it behind the right light,
beckoning toward oneself three times.
This is the mudrā for invitation.
By means of this mudrā, one invites all mantra-deities and summons the Vajradharas.
How much more so for other bodhisattvas and the like.
Throwing the left parasol outward three times is the seal of respectful dismissal.
This is the same as the previous root mudrā;
the two thumbs are bent and pressed against each other,
resting upon the two index fingers.
The two fingers are each placed upright against the side of the lid;
this is the argha mudrā.
First, place a flower within the palm.
Thereafter, one should form this mudrā.
For both the initial invitation and the final dismissal,
one should use this mudrā to offer arghya water.
Using the same root mudrā as before,
bend both wheels (thumbs and index fingers) inward into the palms;
this constitutes the boundary of the cardinal and intermediate directions.
Then, with the two hands in the previous mudrā, hold both wheels upright,
slightly not touching the cover,
and form the seal while gazing upward with the eyes.
This is called the Seal of the Upper Direction.
It is the same as the previous seal, with both wheels held upright,
moving and beckoning alternately to the left and right.
This is called the Seal for Destroying All Crucial Points.
It is the aforementioned Root Seal;
the left and right wheels are covered and each supports the other like a ring.
Each abides according to its own light.

This is called the seal that binds all sentient beings, as well as the Kumāradevas, Brahmādevas, Maheśvaradevas, Nārāyaṇadevas, and others, binding them and summoning them to bring them into submission.
The wheel seal of covering constitutes liberation;
it is the aforementioned fundamental seal.
If one wishes to sever and destroy another’s mantra,
one should place the two wheel-armors against the sides of the two lid-armors;
thus all mantras and vidyās will be severed and destroyed.
This is the same as the previous root mudrā;
however, the right hand is bent and rests beneath the lower joint of the right ray of light.
This is the gandha (scented unguent) mudrā.
This is the same as the previous root mudrā;
bend the left hand into a hollowed cup and rest it against the lower joint of the left thumb.
This is the Flower Seal (Puṣpamudrā).
It is the same as the previously mentioned Root Seal (Mūlamudrā),
with both hands folded so that they rest beneath the lower joints of the two rays.
This is the incense-offering mudrā;
it is the same as the previous root mudrā,
with the two thumbs bent at the first joint.
Each is attached to the side of the two wheels;
this is called the food-offering mudrā,
which is identical to the previously mentioned root mudrā.
Bend the two joints of the two covers so that their backs do not touch each other; then,
stand both wheels upright to press against the sides of the covers.
This is called the Lamp Seal (Dīpamudrā).
The practitioner should bind and employ these seals when performing recitation.
This is the same as the original root mudrā;
with the two thumbs covering the two wheel-armors upon the palms,
this is called "The Binder of All Untamable Ghosts, Demons, Vetālas, Ḍākinīs, and Water-dwellers."
Bind their mouths.
Then, perform the release by forming the seal as in the root mudrā.
Form the root mudrā.
Place flowers and fruits within the mudrā;
by reciting [the mantra] while giving them to others, one will immediately attain their respect and affection.
This is the aforementioned root mudrā.
Bending the two thumbs and first joints so they press against each other,
one should apply pressure with both wheels while reciting the root mantra with wrathful intensity.
It can restrain elephants, horses, and chariot wheels.
By forming this mudrā while riding an elephant and casting it from afar,
one can restrain enemy forces.
Having bound the fundamental mudrā,
one may enter an army formation;
it will be able to restrain all weapons so that one cannot be harmed by them.
Forming the root mudrā,
one wrathfully casts [the mantra] into a pond, well, or spring;
all the nāga palaces are set ablaze with fierce flames.
It slays all nāgas and hurls them into the air;
it can also slay all vidyādharas, ṛṣis, gandharvas, and kiṃnaras.
At that time, the Blessed One again addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
This great maṇḍala is named "Upholder of the Samaya.
It is capable of subduing all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
It cannot be transgressed by any bodhisattva;
it subdues all sentient beings who are difficult to subdue and can destroy all mantras and vidyās.
This phrase summons all bodhisattvas;
it is a great lion’s roar praised and extolled by all Buddhas, bringing them joy.
As soon as one forms this mudrā, even bodhisattvas established on the tenth stage [are summoned].
They all wish to dissolve their alarm and terror;
how much more so for other Brahmās and the like.
Therefore, noble son, I [speak] for your sake and for that of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
This is the Great Lion’s Roar.

Without doubt,

Furthermore, the Dharma also explains other most excellent methods of accomplishment.

All devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and others prostrate to him;
he need not yield the path, for his body is translucent and surpasses ten buddha-fields as he wanders through immeasurable worlds.
Together with a retinue of a thousand, his lifespan shall be one great kalpa;
at the end of life, he will be reborn in the palace of Vajrapāṇi.
Furthermore, for the sake of those who are ill, empower water seven times with this dharma.

If one suffers from possession by a malevolent spirit (*bhūta*), performing a *homa* with white mustard seeds will cause all such spirits to flee and disperse.
Furthermore, there is another method: place an image of the Honored One on the shore of the ocean and recite the mantra one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*) according to the ritual manual.
The Nāga King Sāgara will then cause [the practitioner] to enter his own palace.
Within that, one seeks the wish-fulfilling jewel;
having obtained it, one manifests bodies according to one's desires and acts with complete freedom.
Furthermore, there is a method: install an image of the principal deity in an asura cave and recite [the mantra] one lakh times.
An asura maiden will appear and lead the practitioner inside.
Having entered, one seeks the long-life elixir of the asuras;
some obtain it, while others remain there.
Furthermore, there is a method for begging alms at a single stūpa.
Perform the preliminary rites.
Once the recitation of one hundred thousand repetitions is completed,
on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, abstain from food for a full day and night.
One should offer food and drink according to one's ability and perform recitations until one's own shadow disappears; thereby,
one will attain unsurpassed power and a lifespan of ten thousand years.
If one does not achieve success at first, one should perform the ritual procedures as before and subsequently seek success;
even if one has committed an immediate transgression (ānantarya-karma) by the time of the eighth repetition.
One will likewise achieve accomplishment.
Furthermore, there is a method: wearing a red garland and red garments, and holding a *khaṭvāṅga* in one's hand.
From Śamaśāna, take seven anthills;
construct a stūpa according to the measurement of the Tathāgata’s cubit,
and place the Verse on Dependent Origination before it.
Subsisting on milk and barley, or by begging for alms,
one should sleep before a stūpa and recite one hundred thousand [mantras].
There, one will see various terrifying forms of evil.
One should not be afraid.
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight,
one should fast for a full day and night and perform extensive offerings at a stūpa.
One should bestow food upon all spirits and deities.
One should offer incense, flowers, and burnt offerings to Khataṅga.
Then, donning armor and establishing the boundaries such as the enclosure wall, one sits in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*) and performs the recitation.
Even unto the radiance emerging from the *khataṅka*;
by accomplishing the *khataṅka* and holding it,
one gains respect and affection among the virtuous assembly.
They all followed his instructions.
Then, in another place at night in a secluded spot,
Khaṭvāṅga caused a palace with a hundred pillars to manifest spontaneously upon the ground.
Adorned with all manner of jewels,
celestial maidens attend him, and he follows the instructions of his husband,
accompanied by a retinue of one thousand followers.
All those who delight in it shall have a lifespan of five thousand years;

Furthermore, there is a method: fashion a wheel out of *puṣpa-iron*.
Sharpen the small blades by splitting them to make them keen.
Perform the preliminary rites for the twelve spokes.
Install the image of the principal deity at a site where there is a stūpa containing relics, such as on a riverbank or a mountain peak.

Offer the wheel of blue incense and other substances,

Sitting in the full lotus posture with both hands holding a wheel,

you should not be afraid.
Furthermore, by reciting it again, it becomes a mass of light that surrounds the practitioner;

During that intermediate kalpa, one perceives the appearance of a Buddha in the world;

using the Maṅgala [mantra], protect the body with the One-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa Cakra by reciting the empowerment seven times.
One should summon the nāga Tidri and the vidyādhara Tidri using this same mantra as a hook.
Furthermore, there is another method: take twelve finger-widths of thunderbolt wood and fashion it into a vajra.
Within the śamatha and vipaśyanā,
one should perform three hundred thousand recitations;
thus the gates and bolts of the asuras, both inside and out, will be opened and shattered.
Furthermore, by adding the syllable HŪṂ to the mantra of the One-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa-cakra,

even if one has not yet achieved mastery over the wrathful deity, reciting it will likewise enable one to restrain enemy armies.
If one causes a tree that has been empowered to fall,
it can destroy all vidyās,
mantras, and the syllable HŪṂ.
One obtains protection by reciting [the mantra] within the *śmaśāna*.
Furthermore, there is a method: a blacksmith who has received the eight precepts (*aṣṭāṅga-śīla*) fashions a vajra within the *śmaśāna*.
Having received the eight precepts,
with a mind free from distraction, perform the preparatory rites as previously described;
holding a vajra in hand, recite [the mantra] one million times (ten lakṣas).
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, at midnight,
one should perform the ritual of offering all kinds of incense, flowers, burnt offerings, food, and lamps to the Buddha.
Holding a vajra in the left hand, one should sit in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka) and recite the mantra.
At dawn, the mallet radiates a thousand lights; by holding this mallet,
one immediately attains accomplishment, and together with one's retinue, one soars through the air upon the mere arising of the thought [of awakening],
capable of punishing all vidyādharas.
His majestic radiance is peerless;
together with Śakra, he shares half of his seat as a Great Vidyādhara King,
remaining for one great kalpa.
Holding a vajra, one may travel wherever one pleases.
Furthermore, for conditions such as quartan fever that recurs every four days, as well as spirit-poisons (*gūduka*) and the like,
they shall be dispelled through empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*).
Furthermore, according to another method,
one should fashion an image of Śatru at a śmaśāna and step upon its heart with the left foot.
Pointing with the index finger of the right hand and reciting the one-syllable Uṣṇīṣacakravartin mantra together with the syllable HŪṂ one thousand times,
it will be destroyed in that very instant.
Furthermore, one may also cause it to cease by means of this very mantra.
Another method is to take the ashes of śamī wood and fashion them into the shape of a śatru (enemy).
One should recite the mantra over a *khadira* stake and drive it into the crown of the head;
[the target] will be destroyed instantly.
Furthermore, there is another method: take white mustard seeds.
If one performs the empowerment of śamāśana one hundred thousand times,
one will be able to crush and overturn all keyholes, locks, and the like.
Furthermore, there is another method regarding śamāśana.
On the eighth day, take a *mṛtapuruṣa* (a corpse) that is neither decayed nor damaged;
bathe and adorn it according to the ritual rules,
and offer food to all the spirits and deities of the four directions.
Seated upon the heart, one should cast white mustard seeds into the mouth— one seed for each recitation—
until the great tongue protrudes;
then, cutting it with a sharp blade, it immediately becomes a sword.
By wielding this sword, one becomes a king among all vidyādharas;
possessing incomparable and transcendent power,
one travels at will throughout this world.
Furthermore, there is another method: at a stūpa containing relics, one should offer incense and other items as well as food and drink;
then, on the day of the full moon, one should face the image and perform the offering.
Burn aloeswood incense and perform recitations day and night.
Then, at dawn, invite the monastic community;
you should make offerings to that assembly and request the attainment of *siddhi*.
Then, by means of this ritual manual, one should sit in the full lotus posture and perform recitation;
thereupon, one will achieve the King of Inconceivable [Attainments],
and longevity as well as the power of retention will both be accomplished.
Furthermore, there is a method for performing the preliminary rite:
at a śarīra-stūpa in a pure location,
one should fast for a full day and night on the day of the full moon.
With a mind of earnest devotion, one should take *gomaya* that has not fallen to the ground and smear it upon the altar.
One should take eight jars, fill them with water, various seeds, medicinal herbs, and the like,
and tie diverse flower garlands around their necks.
Mix various incenses— such as kunduruka, tagara, and sandalwood—
with the water contained therein,
and offer it to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, surrendering one’s own body.
Sitting in the full lotus posture,
perform the recitation until light rays emerge from the crown of the head and circle the practitioner clockwise.
He immediately enters the body of the practitioner and attains bodily accomplishment (*kāyasiddhi*).
At that very moment, his body emits light, and in an instant he assumes the appearance of a youth with ringed hair, twenty-eight years of age.
His five supernormal powers (*pañcābhijñā*) and majestic radiance shine like molten gold.
Together with their retinues, they traverse the void;
all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, siddhas,
and mahoragas pay them homage and respect.
In the space of a kṣaṇa, a lava, or a muhūrta, he travels to immeasurable Buddha-worlds;
yet, while practicing the holy life, his mind remains unshakable by desire.
Wherever he goes, the various Śakras there offer him half of their seats.
Possessing incomparable majesty and virtue within the inconceivable Buddha-worlds,
he beheld immeasurable Buddhas;
all the teachings he heard from them, he attained full and resolute understanding.
When practicing the bodhisattva conduct in this sequential manner,
one attains entry into the skillful means of conduct for taming [beings],
rather than relying on the power of those samādhis.
One dwells at ease while diminishing [the afflictions],
and so on until rebirth.
Furthermore, one should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times while immersed in water.
Having performed these rites,
for one who is afflicted by malaria and desires liberation from it,
one should perform a homa with ghee and honey mixed together; thus, one will immediately be cured.
If one performs the rite for pacifying calamities, one should append the syllable *svāhā*.
Furthermore, another method is to place an image of the tutelary deity in a quiet location and [offer] one thousand *kunda* flowers.
Cast the image [into the water] while reciting the name of that person once for each casting;

Furthermore, there is another method for pacifying obstacles and difficulties.
While wearing damp clothes, perform the wrathful recitation.
Burn one hundred and eight offerings of sesame seeds and white mustard seeds mixed with clarified butter three times each day for three days.
All demonic obstacles will be eliminated.
Furthermore, there is a method: ascend to a mountain peak and drink milk;
fashion a vajra twelve or six finger-widths in length using all types of incense.
Holding the mantra rosary in the left hand until warm smoke and light appear:
if smoke appears, one becomes the sovereign among the accomplishments of *anuttara*;
if warmth appears, one holds the vajra, and all whom one beholds will be filled with reverence and affection.

Furthermore, there is a method for taking sūtradharajaṇa:
first, perform a homa of one thousand three hundred pādas.
At the time of a solar eclipse, perform one hundred and eight empowerments (*adhitiṣṭhanā*).
Place it in the mouth and recite until the sun reappears.
Then have a Brahmin woman grind it.
If one consecrates [the substance] one thousand and eight times and applies it to the eyes,
one will immediately attain *āṭopana*.
This is the method for accomplishing all *āṭopana* rites.
One cannot conceal oneself.
Furthermore, regarding the method for seeking the accomplishment of speech:
perform the preliminary rites in a pure place.
Having installed the image of the principal deity, offer food in sequence to all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and so forth.
Before the image, construct a homa hearth and perform one hundred thousand oblations of blue lotuses mixed with the three sweets.
Success is then achieved.
Circumambulate the image of the deity clockwise and perform recitation facing it.
On other days, provide offerings to the Saṅgha according to one's ability and request success.
From this point forward, whatever one desires shall all be obtained in accordance with one's words. Furthermore, there is a method:
prepare pills using agallochum incense (*guggulu*).
Perform one hundred and eight *homa* offerings during each of the three periods;
whatever the mind desires shall be fully accomplished.
For those afflicted by malevolent spirits, tie a consecrated mantra-thread around [the person].
Furthermore, there is a method: [take] sesame seeds and white mustard seeds mixed with clarified butter (*ghṛta*) and perform *homa* before the image for seven days;
whatever is sought shall be attained.
Furthermore, to cause men and women to feel mutual respect and affection,
fashion an image of that person out of wax;
while doing so, recite the One-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa Cakra mantra.
Fill his belly with bitter oil.
Pierce him at the seven joints with seven *maṇḍala* needles.
Roast him over a fire of *khadira* wood while reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times for seven nights; then one shall obtain what is sought.
Furthermore, regarding the rite for causing another to be expelled:
grind red mustard seeds into powder and fashion it into the likeness of that person's severed right foot.
Recite the mantra over charcoal from a *khadira* fire for seven days while performing *homa*,
and one will immediately obtain one's wishes.
Furthermore, this rite brings about the pacification of calamities for oneself.
In a stūpa containing relics, place an image of the principal deity and offer incense,
flowers, and other offerings.
Take a new flask, fill it with scented water together with all medicinal herbs and various jewels.
Recite the empowerment mantra one hundred and eight times.
Tie an uncut piece of silk around the neck of the flask and perform the ritual ablution upon oneself.
One will be freed from all sins and all obstacles and difficulties.
Furthermore, by consecrating agarwood one hundred and eight times with this dharma,
one may hold it in the mouth and converse with others.
One will gain the respect and affection of all.
When debating legal matters in government offices, one will always prevail in speech.
Furthermore, there is a rite: take yellow flowers and [offer them] into a *khadira* fire.
By performing one thousand *homa* offerings of flowers, one obtains one thousand taels of gold.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one fashions the form of another from salt and performs one thousand empowerments and *homa* offerings in a fire of *khadira* wood.
Whatever that person seeks, they shall all obtain respect and affection.
Lord of Secrets, in this manner, all such mundane and supramundane wheel-turning kings and uṣṇīṣas can be accomplished.

Always held in the hands of practitioners, that sin cannot be found;

This vidyārāja accomplishes all activities;
it can extinguish all fears and constantly provides protection,
increasing wealth and grain, and ensuring longevity and freedom from illness.
The eighty thousand species of ghostly lineages are all eliminated.
All those who practice the arts of suppression and sorcery are stilled;
untimely deaths and the fires of poison are entirely brought to rest.
It brings benefit to all sentient beings,
can eliminate all diseases,
and enables one to sever the influence of all malevolent planets.
The heroic lion, out of compassion for all sentient beings,
spoke these words.

I shall now explain its efficacy,
which removes all transgressions and eliminates all illnesses;
you should listen attentively.

he empowers ash to bind the boundaries of the four directions and corners, and empowers water.
Bind all types of malarial fevers by consecrating thread and tying it [around the patient].
Cause oneself and others to eliminate all sins by performing homa with white mustard seeds mixed with clarified butter.
In order to increase one's lifespan,
one should empower *kumuda* flowers and offer them to the Buddha, the World-Honored One.

If one casts [the substance] into the air, one will immediately obtain clear vision of the heavens free from clouds.
Furthermore, there is a method for consecrating water:
by reciting the name of the person in question while they drink it, one causes them to attain respect and affection.

using a branch of the *kunāla* tree, empower it seven times with mantras;
if hail is falling, strike toward it, and the hail will immediately shift away. This same method is also used for malevolent clouds.
Furthermore, there is a method for binding the boundaries of the cardinal and intermediate directions:
use a khadira-wood stake with water or white mustard seeds to bind the vināyakas.
Furthermore, there is a method: by consecrating colored threads of five hues for all illnesses, one causes them to be cured upon wearing them.
All demonic spirits and all illnesses are immediately stilled through *homā*.
By consecrating flowers and fruits, one gains the respect and affection of others.
Furthermore, by consecrating food and drink,
all to whom they are given will likewise gain respect and affection.
Furthermore, by performing the empowerment of an iron stake (*kīla*),
one receives protection from all fears and all obstacles.
Because of this stake, gods, spirits, and *rākṣasas* shall not approach or transgress against it.
One obtains protection from all fears within a boundary of one yojana.
Furthermore, for the method to ward off poison:
empower a thread seven times and tie it to a wooden staff.
All poisons will be neutralized.
By consecrating earth, white mustard seeds, or water with mantras and applying them,
all [afflictions] shall be cured.
For all illnesses, empower five-colored threads one hundred and eight times;
tying them upon the patient will immediately bring about recovery.
Burning aloeswood incense or frankincense can eliminate all types of malaria.
In all places of fear, by reciting this vidyārāja, one attains fearlessness.

empower a white thread seven times;

Furthermore, there is a method for binding the boundaries of the cardinal and intermediate directions using white mustard seeds.

Moreover, by tying a thread empowered for those possessed by hungry ghosts or afflicted by epilepsy, they are healed.

use the branches of the *kunāla* tree and crush the various seals with ashes.
Recite the mantra over a clod of earth seven times to ward off thieves and cast it in the four directions.

then rest before the image.
In a dream, it will reveal all that is good or evil regarding whatever you seek.

all people will come to respect and love one.

empower water one hundred and eight times and use it to smear upon the face.

Good son, I have now briefly explained that all manner of calamities and disasters shall be unable to cause any harm. Why is this?
The realm of the Buddha;
the sphere of activity of immeasurable Buddhas;
the immeasurable Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
"O Lord of Secrets, this 'Play of Immeasurable Samādhis' was taught by the Tathāgatas of this entire Bhadrakalpa;

I now speak it as well;
the Tathāgatas, equal in number to the sands of the Ganges and bearing the same name,

If there are sons or daughters of good family who,
in a future age and at a later time, being bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās,

If one recites and maintains this vidyārāja mantra and achieves its accomplishment, hearing such benefits as these,

If reborn among humans, one shall become a king and attain the wisdom of recollecting past lives.

Chapter Six: The Exposition of the Dharma. *The Sūtra of the One-Syllable Extraordinary Uṣṇīṣa of the Buddha*. Chapter Six: The Exposition of the Dharma. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Śāntamati...
The younger brother of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi rose from that great assembly,
joined his palms, and paid homage to the Buddha.
In order to make an offering to the World-Honored One,
he removed from his own neck a priceless, great pearl necklace and,
holding it with his right hand, presented it to the World-Honored One.
Because it is said that the response is sublime,
he spoke this verse to praise the Buddha:
"O You whose voice is supreme in the three realms, You who gladden the hearts of all sentient beings."
The Buddha’s voice is most supreme; manifesting speech, it attains glory and prosperity.
All Buddhas abide in the Dharma; the Subduer teaches that Dharma.
Those who have attained equal enlightenment through what was taught—the World-Honored One has realized Bodhi.
Those who turn the sublime wheel of Dharma, those Buddhas of the past who have perfected their cultivation—
all sit upon this; the peerless person in the world,
in each and every place, becomes like a vajra.
To behold the Blessed One is auspicious;
it was auspicious in the past. Furthermore, to hear the sublime Dharma is auspicious; that too is likewise auspicious.
Hearing that teaching, they do not falter;
the wise abide therein, always perceiving it as heaven.
They also regard it as their parents, their teachers, and their sisters; thus they see all as those who are fearless.
First, one should practice in accordance with the instructions; in this regard, ethical discipline (*śīla*) is supreme.
By means of it, one relies upon the King of Dharma and receives offerings, just as a garland of *mallikā* flowers, when its fragrance is wafted by the wind, brings delight to the mind.
Just as oil is produced from a mixture of sesame seeds, its fragrance is likewise most fragrant;
so too is your honored one’s color peerless, beyond the calculation of all beings,
profound in depth and majesty, and supreme in name, form, and supernormal powers.
Regarding this very ground that I now behold, how could I conceive of it as high or vast?
As for women and men, if one were to praise even a small virtue,
and if what is heard here is the Dharma, then having heard it, faith shall arise once more.
If there are those who can practice renunciation and giving,
whether they have gone forth from the household life within the teaching of the World-Honored One or remain within the teaching of the Śākya King—
toward all of them, I maintain the thought of compassion as toward my own kin.
Like mosquitoes and gadflies in the sky, like the hoofprints of an ox in the great ocean—such are the Buddha’s virtues;
the praises offered to them are like the words of one dreaming.
As I have here extolled the virtues of the Heavenly King, so too [are they insignificant].
Whether it be the qualities of the Buddha’s voice,
I praise, revere, uphold, and make offerings to them according to my capacity;
by these supreme roots of goodness— such as pearl necklaces and priceless jewels— may all sentient beings become equal to the Buddhas.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Śāntamati,
having praised the World-Honored One with these verses,
addressed the Buddha, saying: "By how many dharmas does a bodhisattva [attain this]?"
When the cultivation of this Uṣṇīṣacakravartin, the samādhi of all Tathāgatas, was fully accomplished and blazing,
the World-Honored One then replied to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Śāntamati with these verses:
If one possesses a compassionate and pure mind, who is not coarse but gentle and endowed with mindfulness;
who guards the prohibitions, is upright, and practices the holy life— such a person accomplishes this vidyārāja,
remains free from fault, does no evil, increases in constant tranquility, and is free from anger.
Such a person becomes a Vidyārāja: one who harbors no resentment toward others nor engages in frivolity;
one who never acts thus toward others and does not look upon the faults or virtues of others—such a person becomes a Vidyārāja, provided they are fully endowed with the merits of the Buddha-dharma.
Always practicing reverence and making offerings, one does not strike others nor disparage them;
all these qualities are accomplished by this Vidyārāja. Free from stinginess, envy, and pride, one does no harm to others, nor does one falsely attribute faults or calamities to them.
"O son of good family who has thus accomplished the King of Mantras, I have served sixty koṭis of Buddhas and made offerings to them;
yet, under those koṭis of Buddhas, I did not practice the holy life."
Seeking the Dharma and practicing with diligence,
he received from him the Great Vidyārāja, which has spread widely.
Through those roots of virtue, he thus attained vast merit, majesty, and power.
"Good son, because the inconceivable samādhis of all Tathāgatas are supreme,
the bodhisattva protects body, speech, and mind,
and practices the One-Syllable Wheel King."
"In this way, son of good family, for all sentient beings, the Tathāgata takes the form of a mantra as a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra).
Śāntamati spoke thus: 'World-Honored One, sons and daughters of good family should revere [the Tathāgata] with the thought that he is a spiritual friend.'"
One should practice the Great Vidyārāja and should serve and make offerings to him.
Why is this, Śāntamati?
If one draws near to and cultivates the practice of spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra),
one will accomplish wholesome qualities and hear sublime teachings;
through a virtuous intention, one then attains wholesome application.
By means of wholesome karma, one proceeds toward the wholesome;
having obtained wholesome companions and not engaging in unwholesome deeds,
one applies oneself to wholesome practice and proceeds toward the wholesome.
By attending upon virtuous companions and refraining from unwholesome deeds,
one does no evil toward others; thus protecting their minds,
one fulfills the path to enlightenment and becomes capable of abiding upon that path.
They possess great power to bring about the welfare of sentient beings dwelling in evil realms; therefore,
Śāntamati, you should associate with virtuous friends.
All merits were brought to complete fulfillment,
and all offered praise.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Śāntamati addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Bhagavān, by accomplishing how many dharmas do bodhisattva-mahāsattvas swiftly realize unsurpassed,
perfect, and complete enlightenment and attain the profound dharma-patience?"

The Buddha told the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Śāntamati: "There are four dharmas, the accomplishment of which leads to the swift realization of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, and the attainment of the profound patience regarding dharmas (gambhīra-dharma-kṣānti)."
What are the four dharmas? They are:
entering the knowledge of dependently arisen phenomena; entering the realization that there is no sentient being, no person, and no life-span;
and attaining a resolute conviction regarding the sphere of the empty nature of phenomena.
It is far removed from the two views of eternalism and nihilism.
These four dharmas are pure in the past limit and do not come from the future limit;
they are equal throughout the three periods of time.
By means of the wisdom of the present, one should contemplate these four dharmas.
Furthermore, there are four other dharmas regarding the Buddha-nature that should be contemplated:
the Buddha’s nature of form, the teaching on the renunciation of the Saṃgha, the Tathāgata, and the purification of the wisdom-eye through the wisdom-eye.
